atoms.b: In the places where the Anglo-Saxons hadn’t settled, Britons continued to follow the religion of ((++Christianity Islam)), which the Romans had brought to the isles.

instruction.text: In AD 597, the Roman Christian Church sent missionaries to Britain, led by a monk called Augustine. Why do you think the Church sent these missionaries?
instruction.sound: In ay d 597, the Roman Christian Church sent missionaries to Britain, led by a monk called Augustine. Why do you think the Church sent these missionaries?

hint.label: Missionary
hint.text: A missionary is someone sent by a church to other places to teach people about their religion.

b.sound: To convert the Anglo-Saxons to Christianity.

instruction.text: This is a conversation between Augustine and King Aethelberht of Kent. Fill in the gaps.
instruction.sound: This is a conversation between Augustine and King Ethelbert of Kent. Fill in the gaps.

hint.text: Augustine founded Canterbury Cathedral, which is one of the most important churches in the UK.
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.b: King Aethelberht, I believe that you and your people should convert to ((++Christianity Paganism)).
atoms.sound: King Ethelbert, I believe that you and your people should convert to Christianity.

atoms.b: Why would I ever do that? I’m happy being a Pagan and believing in my ((++multiple one)) gods and goddesses.
You may be a Pagan, but your wife, Bertha, is a Christian and a good person. If you ((++love hate)) her, you should give Christianity a chance.
Hmm. What other ((++benefits problems)) would converting to Christianity give me?
Converting to Christianity allows you to gain powerful Christian ((++allies enemies)) in Europe.
That does sound ((++good awful)). I will consider converting to Christianity.

finish.text: Anglo-Saxon kings who converted to Christianity also expected the people they ruled to convert. By around AD 700, Christianity became a big part of life and everyone was expected to go to church.
finish.sound: Anglo-Saxon kings who converted to Christianity also expected the people they ruled to convert. By around ay d 700, Christianity became a big part of life and everyone was expected to go to church.

feedback.end: These churches were known as minsters and were set up by kings and noblemen. The priests, monks and nuns of the minster were then expected to pray for them, especially in times of trouble and war.

instruction.text: Once Britain became Christian again, more written texts were available. Why do you think this was the case?

b.sound: There were now monks and nuns who could read and write.
More written texts just appeared out of nowhere.

feedback.end: These are the ruins of Lindisfarne Priory, a monastery on Holy Island off the coast of North-East England. At some time between the late 600s and early 700s, the monks of this monastery created a famous illuminated book, called the Lindisfarne Gospels.

atoms.b: handwritten book with painted decorations and borders.
atoms.sound: An illuminated book is a handwritten book with painted decorations and borders.

atoms.a: The decorations on the Lindisfarne Gospels show ...
atoms.b: Anglo-Saxon art, culture and religious expression.
atoms.sound: The decorations on the Lindisfarne Gospels show Anglo-Saxon art, culture and religious expression.
